images.title: Ink blot on a folded sheet
images.purpose: Show that pressing ink from a folded half prints a mirror picture, so the crease is the line of symmetry.
images.composition: One opened sheet with a crease down the middle, wide space around it.
images.exact_structure: One rectangular sheet 6 cm wide and 4 cm tall, plain with a thin outline. One vertical crease in grey #6B7280 exactly down the middle. One teal #0072B2 blot with a wavy outline on the right of the crease, and its exact mirror copy on the left, touching at the crease, same size. Exactly 1 sheet, 1 crease, 2 blot halves.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a blot that differs between the two sides
images.takeaway: The crease is the line of symmetry of the ink pattern.
images.description: An opened sheet with a vertical crease and a teal ink blot that is the same on both sides of the crease.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say what happens if the sheet is folded on the crease again.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
